gaps.explanation: 'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: He whispered ___ the children wouldn't hear.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + wouldn't' expresses intended (here negative) purpose.

gaps.sentence: I noted down the reference number ___ I needed it later.
gaps.hint: just in case it proved necessary
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = because it might be needed later; no purpose is intended.

gaps.sentence: The drug trial was halted ___ an irregularity in the data.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to' + noun phrase gives the reason in formal register.
